title: The autonomy category error wrapper raises a second exception instead of containing the original failure
observed_behavior: When a category evaluator raises, category_evaluation_error calls autonomy_types.category without its mandatory labels keyword. A current-hash probe raised TypeError: category() missing 1 required keyword-only argument: labels rather than returning the intended review category.
expected_invariant: A failure in one read-only health category must be represented as a bounded review item so the remaining health categories and launch-gate evidence remain available.
root_cause: The shared error wrapper bypasses the local _category helper that supplies AUTONOMY_CATEGORY_LABELS and directly calls category with an incomplete signature.
failure_scenario: A transient stat, JSON, runtime-counter, path-health, or pending-publish read error enters the catch block; the wrapper itself raises and the complete autonomy health request or gate fails instead of degrading only one category.
evidence: autonomy_evaluators.py lines 11-15 catches every evaluator exception and delegates to category_evaluation_error.
Lines 20-37 omit the required labels argument; autonomy_types.category declares labels as keyword-only.
Isolated bundled-runtime probe reproduced the secondary TypeError.
All 110 focused diagnostics tests pass but none injects an evaluator exception through this shared wrapper.
affected_flows: autonomy health gate and soak tooling
existing_safeguards: Each category is intentionally wrapped in try/except and the designed fallback carries a review item with the original message.
safeguard_gap: The fallback object cannot be constructed, so the containment boundary is ineffective precisely on its error path.
tests_missing: Each category evaluator exception returns a review category without raising
The aggregate health payload remains available when one evaluator fails
recommended_remediation: Pass the canonical labels mapping to category or route the fallback through the existing _category helper, then add exception-injection tests for every category entry point.
remediation_risk: low: the change repairs the intended fallback shape without altering healthy-category policy
validation_rung: Focused autonomy-health unit/API tests with injected evaluator failures plus the diagnostics test suite; representative real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current operational failure-path finding; no prior path-local diagnostics finding was present.

title: A failed growth-lock write leaks both the descriptor and an unreleasable lock file
observed_behavior: If os.open succeeds but os.write fails, acquire_growth_snapshot_lock returns (None, error) without closing the acquired descriptor or unlinking the exclusive lock. A disposable probe confirmed lock_exists=true and descriptor_still_open=true after the return.
expected_invariant: Partial lock acquisition must roll back the descriptor and lock artifact before reporting failure, allowing later diagnostic snapshot attempts to proceed.
root_cause: The open and write operations share one try block, but the generic OSError branch has no ownership-aware cleanup for a descriptor created earlier in that block.
failure_scenario: A transient disk, quota, encoding, or filesystem write failure occurs after O_EXCL creation. Every later snapshot attempt times out on the abandoned lock until process exit and manual lock removal, suppressing growth history.
evidence: autonomy_growth.py lines 53-56 acquire then write; lines 61-62 return directly on OSError.
Cleanup exists only in release_growth_snapshot_lock, which the caller cannot use because the failed acquisition returns fd=None.
Injected os.write failure left the actual temporary lock and live descriptor behind.
existing_safeguards: Exclusive creation prevents concurrent writers, acquisition has a timeout, and normal successful use releases in a finally path.
safeguard_gap: The partial-acquisition path loses the ownership token and bypasses the normal release helper.
tests_missing: os.write failure after successful os.open closes and unlinks
A later acquisition succeeds after a partial first failure
recommended_remediation: Track the newly opened fd locally and, on any post-open exception, close it and unlink only the lock created by this attempt before returning the error.
remediation_risk: low: cleanup is limited to a lock artifact this invocation just created
validation_rung: Focused growth-lock fault-injection and reacquisition tests plus the diagnostics suite; representative real media is not required.

title: Duplicate identical storage roots are counted twice in the supposedly unique observed-byte total
observed_behavior: The function excludes nested paths only when parent != path, so two rows resolving to the identical path both contribute their sizes. A probe with two same-path 10-byte rows returned 20.
expected_invariant: The field observed_filesystem_bytes_unique must count each resolved filesystem root once, including exact duplicates as well as nested overlap.
root_cause: The overlap predicate explicitly ignores equal Path values but the input is never deduplicated by resolved identity.
failure_scenario: state_root and local_base resolve to the same directory; growth diagnostics inflate current observed bytes and can report premature budget pressure or a distorted historical trend.
evidence: autonomy_scan.py lines 90-103 normalize all rows but retain duplicates.
The only skip condition requires parent != path.
Current-hash probe returned 20 for two identical 10-byte roots.
existing_safeguards: Paths are resolved and nested child roots are suppressed.
safeguard_gap: Exact identity is the one overlap form not suppressed.
tests_missing: Identical resolved roots contribute once
Equivalent relative and absolute spellings deduplicate
recommended_remediation: Deduplicate normalized paths before summing and define which size wins if duplicate rows disagree, preferably using the maximum or a single canonical scan result.
validation_rung: Focused autonomy-scan/projection tests for identical, nested, and disjoint roots; representative real media is not required.

title: The limited file scan eagerly enumerates and stats the entire directory before applying its limit
observed_behavior: limited_iter_files first materializes list(root.glob(pattern)), then stats and sorts every candidate, slicing only at return. A generator probe with limit=1 consumed all five candidates before returning one.
expected_invariant: A helper presented as a bounded scan must bound filesystem traversal and stat work, or explicitly report that only result cardinality is bounded.
root_cause: The limit is applied after eager collection and full sort rather than through a bounded iterator/top-k algorithm.
failure_scenario: A large runtime directory makes an autonomy health request perform unbounded enumeration and per-entry stat work, causing long stalls or memory pressure despite the configured scan limit.
evidence: autonomy_scan.py line 22 materializes the entire glob; lines 27-34 stat and sort every row; line 36 applies the limit.
Injected five-item generator was fully consumed with limit=1.
The focused diagnostics tests do not assert traversal work bounds.
existing_safeguards: The returned row count is capped and read/stat errors are summarized.
safeguard_gap: The expensive discovery and stat phases are not capped.
tests_missing: Candidate iteration stops at a defined work bound
Large-directory truncation is achieved without full materialization
recommended_remediation: Use streaming bounded selection with an explicit maximum candidates-inspected budget and report both truncation and inspected count.
remediation_risk: medium: preserving newest-first semantics requires a deliberate bounded-selection policy
validation_rung: Focused iterator-consumption tests and a disposable large-directory latency probe; representative real media is not required.

title: Tdarr Matrix bucket summaries count findings as failed cases and mark every selected case as queued
observed_behavior: Each selected row increments queued_count unconditionally, while each warning/error finding increments failed_count. With one selected case and two findings, the result reported selected=1, queued=1, failed=2, passed=0.
expected_invariant: Case-state counts must be mutually coherent and case based: failed_count cannot exceed selected_count, and queued_count must represent cases actually awaiting execution.
root_cause: The aggregation has no case-key deduplication or execution-state input; it substitutes finding cardinality for failed-case cardinality and selection for queue state.
failure_scenario: A case emits multiple findings, producing impossible failure totals and misleading progress/triage metrics in the diagnostics console.
evidence: tdarr_matrix_console.py lines 384-385 increment selected and queued together.
Lines 391-417 count every severe finding as a separate failed bucket unit.
Current-hash probe reproduced failed_count=2 for selected_count=1.
existing_safeguards: Severity and finding totals are retained separately and passed_count is clamped to zero.
safeguard_gap: Clamping hides the impossible arithmetic instead of preserving case identity and state.
tests_missing: Multiple findings on one case count one failed case
Completed and queued states are derived from worker/run evidence
Bucket counts remain internally consistent
recommended_remediation: Aggregate findings by stable case key, derive queued/completed/failed state from run artifacts, and keep finding_count independent from case counts.
remediation_risk: medium: the console contract and WebView rendering may consume these fields
validation_rung: Focused console aggregation/API tests with multi-finding cases and mixed run states; representative real media is not required.

title: A valid Tdarr evidence-open request lets opener failures escape the structured command boundary
observed_behavior: Path validation errors and a missing opener return command-result envelopes, but opener(path) executes outside either guard. A valid-path probe with an opener raising OSError propagated the exception.
expected_invariant: A backend command surface must return one structured failure result for all expected OS/open failures after request validation.
root_cause: The try/except covers only tdarr_matrix_evidence_path; the actual side effect at line 714 is unguarded.
failure_scenario: The target disappears, loses association, or the desktop opener fails; the Local API/controller receives an exception instead of an actionable command result and journal entry.
evidence: tdarr_matrix_console.py lines 692-703 contain path-resolution errors and lines 704-713 handle missing opener.
Line 714 invokes a callable opener without containment.
Injected OSError escaped unchanged.
existing_safeguards: Target names and paths are allowlisted and containment checked before the opener runs.
safeguard_gap: Operational OS failure after validation has no structured translation.
tests_missing: Callable opener OSError returns ok=false command result
Unexpected opener exception is logged/contained consistently
recommended_remediation: Wrap the opener call and return the same structured error envelope with the resolved path and safe error text; retain path allowlisting.
validation_rung: Focused command/service/API tests with opener OSError and missing-target races; representative real media is not required.

title: The operator-required failure count blocks only after exceeding the configured threshold
observed_behavior: The operator-required branch uses > while the infrastructure threshold uses >=. With the configured block count of 10 and exactly 10 operator-required findings, the category returned review with zero blockers.
expected_invariant: A value named and configured as a block count should block when the count reaches the threshold, consistently with the adjacent infrastructure policy.
root_cause: An off-by-one comparison at line 261 contradicts the threshold semantics used elsewhere in the same function.
failure_scenario: Exactly the configured maximum unresolved operator-required failures are present, yet unattended launch remains at review rather than blocked until an eleventh artifact appears.
evidence: autonomy_health_publish.py line 261 uses len(operator_required) > policy.failure_operator_required_block_count.
Line 286 uses >= for the parallel infrastructure threshold.
Current-hash probe at count=10/threshold=10 returned status=review and blocker_count=0.
existing_safeguards: Old operator-required artifacts can independently block by age and counts above the threshold do block.
safeguard_gap: The exact boundary value is permitted despite the configured block-count meaning.
tests_missing: Threshold-minus-one reviews, exact threshold blocks, threshold-plus-one blocks
recommended_remediation: Use >= and add boundary tests, or rename/document the setting as an allowed-count limit if the current comparison is intentional.
remediation_risk: low: one launch-gate boundary changes and should be called out to operators
validation_rung: Focused autonomy failure-category boundary tests plus diagnostics suite; representative real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current high-risk-path threshold finding awaiting independent attestation.

title: Every oversized state file is offered an event-journal archive action even when that route cannot remediate it
observed_behavior: The journals category scans event_file, completed_manifest_path, queue_snapshot_path, progress_file, and log_file, then attaches journal_archive_action(path) to every oversized item. The action is fixed to Archive Event Journal and /api/maintenance/archive-state-journals. A completed.jsonl probe received that unrelated action while its evidence_path still named completed.jsonl.
expected_invariant: A recovery action attached to a blocker must actually target the named artifact, or the blocker must provide a review-only next step with no inapplicable mutation route.
root_cause: A heterogeneous state-file loop reuses one event-journal-specific action factory without discriminating file role; the factory records the supplied path only as evidence, not as the route target.
failure_scenario: completed manifest, queue snapshot, progress, or log exceeds the limit; the operator follows the offered action, archives only the event journal, and the original launch blocker remains while unrelated evidence is mutated.
evidence: autonomy_health_support.py _journal_paths returns five heterogeneous state paths.
autonomy_health_storage.py lines 218-239 attaches _journal_archive_action(path) to all of them.
autonomy_recovery.py lines 52-65 hard-code the event-journal route and label.
Disposable completed-manifest probe reproduced the mismatched route/action.
existing_safeguards: The action requires confirmation, is backend owned, and declares that it does not mutate media.
safeguard_gap: Confirmation cannot make an action applicable to an artifact the backend route does not target.
tests_missing: Each oversized state-file role receives a matching recovery action or none
Executing the suggested action clears the specific blocker
recommended_remediation: Attach journal_archive_action only to the resolved event journal; define separate backend-owned recovery actions for other state roles only where safe, otherwise provide explicit review guidance without a command.
remediation_risk: medium: recovery UI/action inventories and route contracts may need coordinated updates
validation_rung: Focused per-file-role autonomy tests, maintenance archive route tests, and WebView action rendering; representative real media is not required.

title: A failed background metadata write is reported as success and makes close-readiness miss the active process
observed_behavior: The service starts Popen, then silently swallows OSError while writing the only *.process.json identity record and still returns success=true/background_started=true. An end-to-end disposable probe forced that write failure and the production close-evidence scanner returned status=inactive, active_work=false while the mocked child was reported started.
expected_invariant: After a background child starts, failure to persist lifecycle identity must be fail-closed: the start command must report an actionable failure and close-readiness must continue to treat the process as active/unknown until reconciled.
root_cause: Process creation precedes proof persistence; the persistence exception is discarded, and the close scanner/guard discover background work solely by enumerating persisted *.process.json records.
failure_scenario: Disk/quota/ACL/IO failure prevents metadata creation after a real audit child starts. The UI says the run started, then close-readiness sees no metadata and allows application close/shutdown while work is active, losing lifecycle control and durable stdout/stderr ownership evidence.
evidence: tdarr_matrix_audit.py lines 349-357 start the child before metadata persistence.
Lines 367-373 swallow metadata OSError; lines 374-391 return success.
core/processes/tdarr_background.py lines 74-80 and 116 return inactive when the metadata directory has no process files.
core/processes/guard_facade.py lines 219-234 blocks only active/unavailable and permits inactive.
Current-hash call-chain probe returned start_success=true, metadata_exists=false, close_status=inactive, close_active_work=false.
Independent current-hash review was commissioned for this P1 before final disposition.
existing_safeguards: Persisted metadata includes PID/start-time identity, unreadable or invalid existing metadata fails closed, and live persisted processes block close.
safeguard_gap: There is no fail-closed representation for the interval/process whose metadata file could not be created at all.
tests_missing: Metadata write failure after Popen does not return success
Close-readiness remains blocked/unknown after partial start
Partial-start cleanup or durable fallback evidence is validated
recommended_remediation: Create and durably verify a reserved lifecycle record before launch, update it atomically with PID/start identity after launch, and on any post-Popen persistence failure return failure while retaining fail-closed in-memory/durable evidence and attempting controlled child termination/reconciliation.
remediation_risk: high: process start, shutdown, PID identity, and crash recovery must remain consistent across Windows and non-Windows paths
validation_rung: Focused fault-injection and close-readiness tests covering prelaunch reservation, post-Popen metadata failure, termination/reconciliation, stale PID identity, and app close; representative real media is not required, but a disposable real child process is required for remediation validation.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current P1 process-lifecycle finding; distinct independent current-hash attestation is required and in progress.

title: Days-to-exhaustion subtracts observed storage from already-current free space
observed_behavior: minimum_free_bytes is built from current free-space rows, but the projection computes remaining_bytes = minimum_free - current_observed before dividing by growth rate. With current free=1000, observed=100, and growth=100/day, it reported 9 days instead of 10.
expected_invariant: Time-to-exhaustion should divide current available/free bytes (or bytes above an explicit reserve) by projected daily consumption without subtracting unrelated already-used bytes again.
root_cause: The calculation treats minimum_free_bytes as a total capacity/budget even though _growth_storage_roots populates it from current free_space_gb.
failure_scenario: Operators receive systematically premature or zero-day exhaustion estimates as observed state grows, even when ample current free space remains.
evidence: autonomy_health_projection.py lines 287-313 derive free_bytes from current free_space_gb.
Lines 350-357 subtract current_observed from that free-space value.
One-day history probe reported 9.0 days for 1000 current free bytes at 100 bytes/day.
existing_safeguards: Negative growth is clamped, no-history cases avoid a projection, and current raw free-space rows remain present.
safeguard_gap: The derived headline forecast uses incompatible units/semantics despite valid inputs.
tests_missing: Known free-space/growth fixture yields mathematically correct days
Reserve semantics are explicit and tested
recommended_remediation: Define the exhaustion target explicitly and compute days from current free bytes minus any reserve threshold, never from observed-state bytes; rename payload fields if needed.
remediation_risk: low: diagnostic forecast arithmetic only, though downstream display expectations must be updated
validation_rung: Focused projection tests with known current free, reserve, growth, zero-growth, and overlapping-root cases; representative real media is not required.

title: A disappearing worker-result file can crash Tdarr run progress construction
observed_behavior: Glob errors are caught, but every discovered result is then statted in one unguarded list comprehension. A probe returning one path whose stat raised OSError propagated the exception.
expected_invariant: Read-only progress diagnostics must tolerate normal file disappearance/inaccessibility races by skipping or warning on individual artifacts.
root_cause: The exception boundary ends before the per-result stat phase at line 456.
failure_scenario: A worker result is cleaned, replaced, or temporarily inaccessible between glob and stat; the entire diagnostics run-summary/API request fails instead of returning partial progress with a warning.
evidence: tdarr_matrix_console.py lines 439-442 contain only glob enumeration.
Line 456 stats every result without per-path handling.
Injected result-vanished OSError escaped from _run_progress_summary.
All focused diagnostics tests pass without a stat race case.
existing_safeguards: Enumeration OSError is contained and zero-result progress has a valid fallback.
safeguard_gap: The common post-enumeration race is outside that containment.
tests_missing: One result disappearing during stat returns partial progress and warning
All results unstatable returns a stable zero/unknown progress state
recommended_remediation: Stat each result under per-path OSError handling, retain valid mtimes, and expose skipped/error counts or warnings in the run metadata.
validation_rung: Focused run-progress race/error tests plus diagnostics service/API tests; representative real media is not required.
